issues.body: `_model_container_binds` recognizes mount options only when the flag and specification appear as literal whitespace-delimited source tokens. `_run_headless_harness` can assign, for example, `local registry_flag=--volume registry_spec="$SCRIPT_DIR/..:/registry"` and then place `"$registry_flag" "$registry_spec"` in the initial `container=(...)` array. This is valid shell: Docker receives a writable bind of the registry checkout, but the awk scanner ignores the assignments and expansions, still emits exactly the four expected records, and the `container+=(` assertion still sees one append. Thus the model can gain write access to the script later executed with `REGISTRY_SECRETS_PAT` while every added containment row remains green. The new synthetic fixture covers literal Docker mount syntaxes, not the shell composition seam identified in round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Validate the effective argv passed to Docker, or tightly constrain and structurally validate every construct that can produce elements of the launcher array, including variable/array/function/command-substitution expansion. Add a valid, non-crashing mutant that builds `--volume` and its specification in variables and expands them into the initial `container` array, and require the containment assertion to fail. A lexical inventory of literal Docker spellings cannot establish an exact runtime argv contract.
issues.title: Exact mount assertion still misses shell-composed Docker arguments

verdict.summary: The round-3 blocker remains unchanged. `_model_container_binds` still lexically scans whitespace-delimited literal tokens in the source of `_run_headless_harness`; it does not validate the container argv after shell expansion. A mount flag and bind specification can therefore be assigned to ordinary shell variables and expanded as elements of the initial `container=(...)` array. Docker receives the writable registry mount, while the scanner skips both the assignments and expansions, the expected four records remain unchanged, and the separate `container+=(` count remains one. The added syntax fixtures comprehensively exercise literal Docker spellings, but they do not exercise shell argument construction, so the claimed exact filesystem-view assertion is still incomplete. This is materially the same blocker at the same severity as round 3, therefore progress is stagnant.
